seo.title: Students leading change through service | St Luke's Grammar School
seo.description: Two of our Junior School students are putting service into action through the SchoolAid Kids Ambassador Team program.

image.alt: A student in a blue blazer presenting beside a SchoolAid poster

sections.title: Young leaders making a difference in our community
sections.body:
Two of our Junior School students are putting service into action through the SchoolAid Kids Ambassador Team program.

This year, Ethan and Rachel have worked alongside their staff mentors, Mrs Paterson, Mr Chilton and Mrs Lebic, to plan and lead community outreach initiatives across the Dee Why Junior School.

During Terms 2 and 3, their focus has been supporting The Salvation Army through a series of fundraising activities, including mufti days, bake sales and donation drives.

Together, the St Luke’s community has already raised an impressive $5,116, with more fundraising planned through PJ Day.

sections.title: Finding their voice
sections.body:
The KAT Program has also given Ethan and Rachel opportunities to develop as young leaders.

They have created presentations and posters, spoken at assemblies and chapel services, hosted guest speakers and encouraged their classmates to think about the importance of serving others.

Recently, Ethan represented St Luke’s at the IPSHA Social Expo at St Ignatius’ College Riverview. He confidently delivered part of the SchoolAid KAT Program presentation before being selected from the audience to respond to questions from the Master of Ceremonies.

These experiences are helping our students develop the confidence to communicate, collaborate and lead, while understanding that even small actions can make a meaningful difference.

quote.text: They have inspired fellow students to appreciate the importance and impact of community outreach.
quote.name: Mrs Lebic

sections.title: Service starts with us
sections.body:
At St Luke’s, service is part of developing the whole person. Through opportunities to support others, students learn that leadership isn't simply about having a title. It's about noticing where help is needed, taking responsibility and having the courage to make a difference.

Congratulations to Ethan and Rachel on their leadership, initiative and commitment to serving others.
